profile.address: Lookout Drive, Garland, Dallas County, Texas, 75044
profile.reading: This point is one of four building footprints OpenStreetMap contributors have mapped as NTT in a roughly 600-meter cluster just south of Lookout Drive in Garland, TX, the same street NTT's own site gives for its confirmed Dallas TX1 (2008 Lookout Dr, 230,000 square feet, 16 megawatts of critical IT load, with SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIST 800-53 High, and HIPAA attestations) and Dallas TX4 (2060 Lookout Dr, 127,000 square feet, 36 megawatts, part of a 124-megawatt planned campus, available from June 2026) buildings; data center directory Baxtel additionally lists TX2 at 2108 Lookout Dr and TX3 at 2080 Lookout Dr. An earlier reverse-geocoding pass on this point's own coordinates returned a nearby but unrelated street name (matching Atlas Crown Apartments), which this entry does not repeat as a confirmed address; a direct comparison of this way's own node coordinates against NTT's documented Lookout Drive buildings instead places it within the same tight campus cluster as the other three mapped NTT buildings in this immediate area. Because this way lacks an address or building-reference tag of its own, this entry cannot confirm which specific NTT building (TX1, TX2, TX3, or TX4) it corresponds to, and does not guess; it is presented as part of the shared Garland, TX data center campus rather than assigned a false building-specific address or capacity figure. RagingWire (NTT's US brand) announced this campus in 2022 as a planned 1-million-square-foot, 80-megawatt-plus development, since expanded further per the individual building figures above.

reading.body:
NTT has announced a planned 124 MW IT load campus in the Dallas area, comprising at least two buildings designated TX1 and TX4. The operator has not published the street address, completion date, or current operational status of either building. The specific location remains unconfirmed, though the campus is known to sit in or near Garland or Richardson in Dallas County, Texas.

At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 124 MW of IT load would support roughly 3,100 racks. This would place the Dallas campus among the largest published capacities in Texas, though the state context shows only 18 of 133 mapped facilities in Texas publish megawatt figures at all, making rankings uncertain. The published total for Texas is 468 MW across those 18 facilities, so a full 124 MW campus would represent 21 percent of the state's disclosed capacity.

No certifications, power supply terms, cooling approach, or grid interconnection details are published for this campus. The research status is complete, meaning no further confirmation of the address or specifications is expected from public sources. Whether this capacity is currently built, under construction, or planned only remains unknown from the operator's disclosed information.
